Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

hug verb

also embrace, hug each other

classical

amplector, amplectī

verb, third conjugation, deponent

embrace or hug

Other words

  • complector, complectī, complexus sum — embrace, hug

    verb, third conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Traupman 330

  • amplexor, amplexārī, amplexātus sum — hug, hold in one’s arms, cuddle

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Plaut. Asin. 619: num fūmus est haec mulier quam amplexāre?; Plaut. Asin. 739: patrem hanc amplexārī tuom?

    The frequentative of amplector: mostly ante-classical and in Cicero (Lewis & Short).

  • amplexus, amplexūs m. — an encircling, an embrace

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Liv. 36.17: ōceanus, quī orbem terrārum amplexū fīnit (Lewis & Short); Ov. Met. 9.52 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Vīs ut tē amplectar?

    Would you like a hug?composed

  • Tē amplector.

    I’m hugging you.composed

  • inter sē complectī

    to hug each otherTraupman 330

  • Ere, salvē. Sed num fūmus est haec mulier quam amplexāre?

    Hello, master. But is that woman you’re hugging made of smoke?Plaut. Asin. 619

  • ōceanus, quī orbem terrārum amplexū fīnit

    the ocean, which bounds the circle of the earth with its embraceLiv. 36.17 (Lewis & Short)

See also lap, hold in one’s arms, kiss, comfort.

SourcesLewis & Short: amplector · Lewis & Short: complector · Lewis & Short: amplexor
